scope: Retrospective timing study on the original 1,100-call dataset. Preserve each saved day's entry/cohort filter, sizing, fees, volume limits and exit. Vary the wait after that filter's completed first minute. These dates have been repeatedly examined; this is not fresh validation. Frozen forward candidates are unchanged.
selection: For each source procedure and evaluation day, use only outcomes fully observed before its existing cutoff. Choose among seven nominal waits. Require positive training return at both 5% and 10% sale costs, ten trades/eight contracts and the stated drawdown ceiling. Latency selectors require every 0/1/2/5/10-second added delay to pass and maximize the worst 10%-cost return. Robust selection requires fourteen trades/ten contracts/three trading dates and positive return without two best tokens and without the best entry day at every lag. Ties retain the earlier catalog wait; cash is allowed.
execution: At least one second after first-minute features are known. Market fill at the first observed second within ten seconds. Preserve the existing delayed exit, fee reserve, $1,000 account, 1% pre-call volume limit, one-position and one-trade-per-contract assumptions. Pre-call fee and capacity estimates stay fixed and may be stale for longer waits. These are price-path scenarios, not measured execution latency or AMM fills.
